label: Segmented Track
title: Segmented Track
summary: Use a Segmented Track to show how one whole splits into a few parts, such as a portfolio’s equity, debt, and cash.
corePrinciple: Parts of one whole, sized by their share and named in a legend.

anatomy.title: A rounded track split by share
anatomy.description: The track is a 24 px bar with fully rounded ends. Each slice’s width is its share of the total, and the colours step from strong to light.
blocks: Rounds the ends and holds the slices with no gaps.
Strongest colour; its width is its share.
A lighter step of the same colour.
Lightest; the steps repeat after three slices.

configuration.title: Shares and appearance
configuration.description: Pass each part’s share; the track works out the widths. An appearance recolours every slice. Figma and code both default to Senary gold.
blocks: Without shares every slice is the same width, as in Figma.
After three slices the colours repeat, so the legend tells them apart.

examples.title: Five parts
examples.description: After three slices the colours repeat, so the legend tells them apart.

states.title: Display only
states.description: Segmented Track has no hover, pressed, selected, or disabled state and can’t take focus. Only the data changes it, so pass real shares and hide the track when there are none.
blocks: A part worth 0 still draws a 1 px sliver; leave it out instead.
An empty list draws an empty 24 px track; hide the track instead.

examples.title: A zero share
examples.description: A part worth 0 still draws a 1 px sliver; leave it out instead.

examples.title: No data
examples.description: An empty list draws an empty 24 px track; hide the track instead.

sizing.title: 24 px tall, full width
sizing.description: The track is 24 px tall with fully rounded ends and stretches to the width of its container. Slices share that width by their shares, with no gaps.

content.title: Name the mix and every part
content.description: The track has no text, so give it a spoken name that lists the shares, such as “Portfolio mix: equity 60%, debt 25%, cash 15%”, and put a legend with the same names next to it. Use short names in sentence case and plain percentages.

inContext.title: A portfolio card
inContext.description: The screen works out each part’s share and passes the same list, in the same order, to the track and the legend, so their colours match. Nothing on the track is pressable; to switch between mixes, use Range Track, which adds tabs.

doDont.title: Show one whole, clearly named
doDont.description: Each pair shows a track people can read versus one that misleads them.
blocks: Equity, debt, and cash add up to the portfolio.
Use it as a progress bar
One value filling a track is a progress bar, not a split.
Each name and share sits next to its colour.
Without a legend nobody knows which slice is which.
All three slices turn the same grey and the split disappears.
Hide it when there’s no data
It leaves a blank gap that says nothing about why.

sources.title: Use the public Segmented Track contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (12 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Segmented Track is one 268 × 24 component with three equal gold slices, the Senary appearance, which code now uses by default too. It is display-only: on the web it is a group named by its spoken name, and a slice given its own name is read as an image inside that group. Range Track builds on it, adding tabs and a legend. The published Storybook predates 0.1.78.
